scope: Finite-cap exact calibration of paired Bernoulli discordance-sign boundaries, H=2048 and delta=.01. No simulation observations, no changes to frozen prior rounds.
main_conclusion: Finite-horizon binomial absorbing-state calibration, Beta mixture boundaries, mixture SPRTs, and optimized alpha spending all have direct prior art. A new certified implementation can be valuable but these principles are not an originality claim or a demonstrated international-leading result.

primary_sources.title: Sequential: Exact Sequential Analysis for Poisson and Binomial Data
read_scope: Performance.Threshold.Binomial.R core statistic and absorption recursion
Optimal.Binomial.R inputs, constraints, objective and output
findings: Exact finite-horizon sequential binomial critical values and arbitrary integer-boundary operating characteristics are standard implemented functionality.
Manual p81 claims CV.Binomial accepts upper/lower/two tails, but current source explicitly rejects any Tailed other than upper in both continuous and group branches.
Performance.Threshold.Binomial has a real two-sided branch and can evaluate supplied integer lower/upper boundaries under p=.5.

official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.statistic: For p0=1/(1+z), LLR(D,K)=D KL(K/D,p0) when K/D>p0 and 0 otherwise; K=D uses D log(1+z). No factor 2.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.crossing: LLR >= cv, not strict >; integer upper absorption boundary is first K satisfying this and K>=M.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.minimum_events: M defaults to 1 and is the minimum number of upper-side successes, not a minimum total D; some early impossible looks are suppressed.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.groups: GroupSizes defaults to 1, testing at each D; a group vector tests at cumulative group sizes and must sum to N.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.cap: N is a positive integer. There is no N<=1000 hard check in CV.Binomial source; manual p80 recommends <=1000 for runtime. N=2048 was not executed in R.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.critical_value_search: Searches ordered attainable floating LLR values with a binomial Markov recursion. Final cv is rounded upward to 5 decimals (line174); compare resulting integer absorbing states rather than expecting identical float thresholds.
official_CV_Binomial_source_crosswalk.numerical_scope: Official exact means exact-distribution computation, not arbitrary-precision outward arithmetic. Our dyadic path-count certificate should independently certify the frozen integer table.

official_two_sided_evaluator.note: At p=.5 its two-sided LLR is D KL(K/D,.5), including symmetric endpoints. Supplied integer boundaries avoid float threshold conversion.

small_reference_check.official_published_example: Manual p82 example N25,alpha.05,M1,z7/2,GroupSizes5 has cv1.9852 and displayed risk.04775995; independent integer transition calculation gives .04775995282015197.
small_reference_check.scope: Exact integer/rational probability of the included boundary tables. Symmetric tables are a transparent mathematical extension; no R package code was executed.

comparison_contract: All finite-budget methods use the same H=2048 discordances, delta=.01 and every-D eligibility, with a physical cap of4096 shots.
A physical pair costs2 shots whether concordant or discordant; calibrating in D never makes concordant observations free.
Freeze exact integer rejection states, including tie and terminal behavior. Floating statistics can propose shapes; exact path counts certify the actual table.
Cap without a directional crossing is abstain for every comparator. It is not evidence accepting a nonpositive or negative sign.
Count wrong decisions and cap abstentions in unconditional cost, and report each separately.
Finite-horizon thresholds cannot be continued beyond H without a newly justified risk contract; retain an infinite-horizon baseline if such flexibility is a product requirement.
Selecting an effect, prior or boundary after viewing evaluation outcomes is development selection, not held-out superiority.

Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.ESampleSize: Source lines367-383 includes N*(1-power), matching capped nonrejection cost in Bernoulli-event units.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.ETimeToSignal: Source divides signal-time sum by power; this conditions on signaling and does not match unconditional capped cost.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.two_sided_design: Requires two fixed alternatives RR[1]<1<RR[2] and two target powers. Its objective averages the two alternative-specific measures, not every unknown effect.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.unknown_alternative: No single quoted LP optimum applies to a heterogeneous unknown-effect benchmark without a prespecified prior, minimax objective, or matched power constraints.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.physical_cost_mismatch: The Bernoulli-event horizon is not the same as a fixed physical-pair horizon with a random nuisance-dependent discordance count; physical expected shots need a separate matched objective.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.directional_errors: Equality-null two-sided rejection is not by itself a uniform directional-error theorem; a monotone-boundary coupling argument must be checked for the returned stopping rule.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.randomization_and_numerics: The inspected LP source uses continuous solution variables and a numerical simplex solver. A rounded nonrandomized integer boundary cannot inherit claimed LP optimality automatically; certify its actual risk and recompute cost/power.
Optimal_Binomial_scope_for_FaultTune.size_limits: Manual says continuous N<=240. Current source lines122-124 sets Nref300 when the supplied GroupSizes length<=20 and Nref240 otherwise, then rejects N>Nref. It cannot run H2048 unchanged.

Global minimum physical shots over all effects
The validity or optimality of an uninspected randomized LP decision rule after conversion to our directional-abstention protocol

Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.pairwise_m1_identity: For one Bernoulli observation per side, conditioning on a discordance gives a fair sign under equality. Each fixed Fisher odds expert is a Bernoulli sign LR; its mixture depends only on(D,K). The Beta+pair_grid mixture is therefore eligible for the same symmetric-table DP.
Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.larger_blocks: For m>1 Fisher factors depend on each block total as well as cumulative sign; past block totals change the accumulated CGF. The full process is not a function of(D,K) alone.
Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.conditional_nuisance_limit: Conditioning retrospectively on an entire future block-total sequence is not automatically valid under adaptive actions or probabilities; future totals can depend on prior signs. An exact finite-horizon guarantee needs the appropriate joint or worst-case conditional-state recursion.
Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.invalid_shortcut: Replacing the original hedge threshold100 by a smaller Beta-only calibrated threshold, or scaling the Beta capital before adding it to the Fisher e-value, has no inherited hedge guarantee.
Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.simple_valid_alternative: Use an OR of separately valid Beta finite-boundary and Fisher original-boundary decisions with delta_beta+delta_fisher=delta, predeclared conflict handling and no post-hoc risk split. This is a new combined stopping protocol, not the old arithmetic hedge.
Fisher_and_hedge_fair_upgrade.scope_of_original_false_stop: The prior development fine-block hedge false stop remains preserved. Recalibration does not erase that observation or demonstrate a nominal-risk violation from one event.
